problem_type: MCP credential handoff discoverability and silent host-config repair
symptom: A client asks for a provider key but Nomi stays behind other windows and the user must find Settings manually; a stale Nomi-owned host config can be repaired at boot without telling the user to restart the assistant that still holds the old entry.
direct_cause: integration.open_credentials only enqueues a durable handoff and the startup repair result is discarded, so neither path has an application-visible navigation or notification signal.
class_root: Shared boundaries do not propagate user-actionable effects after durable credential/config state changes: GUI focus/navigation and changed repair state are missing from the owning process contract.
affected_population: MCP clients using URL or form-only elicitation
Nomi users with a stale Nomi-owned Claude/Codex/Cursor config
macOS and other Electron desktop platforms
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an app-owned Electron/renderer contract; MCP protocol behavior is already covered by existing tests and is not changed.
invariants: A GUI-owned credential handoff focuses/shows the main window and dispatches the model-settings navigation after the handoff is durable.
A headless or unreachable GUI never claims the window was opened and retains an actionable startup instruction.

Host-config repair reports changed=true exactly when a Nomi-owned file was rewritten; only that signal emits the restart toast, and the toast names every client that was actually rewritten rather than one hard-coded assistant.
generality_proof: All integration.open_credentials calls converge through dispatcher dispatch and GUI RPC dispatch; both URL-capable and form-only clients therefore receive the same focus/navigation side effect. All automatic config migrations converge through repairStaleMcpConfigs, so changed is derived at the shared write boundary rather than from a client-specific caller.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Persist the handoff, then invoke the optional GUI navigation callback before returning the projection.
Own GUI callback wiring and propagate changed host-config repair to the renderer.
Return an explicit changed flag for every rewritten Nomi-owned host config.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: This is the running-app path used by mcpNodeLauncher when an instance advertisement is live.
No GUI exists in this process; callback is absent and existing manual copy remains the honest fallback.
Panel inspection and startup repair share clientInfo migration and the same atomic write boundary.

recurrence.reason: Any supported MCP client can lack URL presentation or any future launch can encounter a stale Nomi-owned entry; the current behavior is structural.
same_class_scan: rg integration.open_credentials across dispatcher, mcpStdioServer, mcpNodeLauncher and UX journeys
rg repairStaleMcpConfigs across appIntegration and mcpConfig tests
inspect handoffQueue consumer in OnboardingDrawer and SettingsDialog navigation

prevention.invariant: Every GUI-owned open_credentials handoff triggers the same renderer navigation callback after durable enqueue; every config repair reports its actual write delta.
prevention.failure_mode: Renderer unavailable rejects the callback and MCP retains the existing manual/startup text; unchanged configs produce changed=false and no toast.
prevention.strategy: Make the durable state transition and its user-facing effect one shared dispatch boundary, with explicit capability absence instead of caller guesses.

legacy_paths.rationale: Existing durable handoff and atomic migration paths remain the canonical paths; this change adds their missing effect signals.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the application-owned callback or repair contract.

migration: No persisted schema migration is needed. Existing handoff/config files are read unchanged; only runtime return shape and effect wiring change.
residual_risks: A GUI that exits between handoff enqueue and renderer acknowledgement still relies on the durable queue and will replay on next settings-open.
macOS focus behavior is verified in the Electron walk-through environment; other window managers retain show/focus best effort semantics.
